elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Revised 21.1: "each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the event" — bilateral by its terms, and no residual unlimited-Customer-liability language survives.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1 uses "Fees actually paid" (not "paid or payable") and contains no USD 1,000,000 floor and no "greater of" construction; the anchor is also "the event" rather than the claim. To reach preferred, redraft as "the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000."

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 21.2: "Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages..." — mutual and untouched by the edit.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.1 now opens "Except for Excluded Claims", and 21.3 defines Excluded Claims to include "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims expressly covers "data-protection, or security obligations", which the new 21.1 carve-out lifts out of the cap.
21.3 includes "its indemnification obligations" within Excluded Claims; 21.1's "Except for Excluded Claims" removes them from the cap (the prior "without exception" override is deleted).
21.3 Excluded Claims: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud"; excepted from the 21.1 cap.
21.3 lists "wilful misconduct" among Excluded Claims, which 21.1 now excepts from the cap.
21.3 lists "fraud" among Excluded Claims, excepted from the revised 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 includes "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" in Excluded Claims, now excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 only says "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages". "Fees" under s.1.5 excludes taxes, reimbursable expenses, interest and any one-time implementation charge, and the sentence is further narrowed to undisputed amounts for conforming Services — a subset, not Customer's payment obligations as a whole. Repair by amending 21.3 to "Customer's obligations to pay any amounts due under this Agreement are not damages and are not limited by this Section."

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Revised 21.1 caps "each Party's aggregate liability"; symmetrical on its face.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Revised 21.1: "Fees actually paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the event" — a 12-month fee basis; "Fees" per s.1.5 is recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap is not illusory. "Actually paid" versus "paid or payable" is a preferred-level shortfall only.
"Except for Excluded Claims" in 21.1 plus 21.3's "its indemnification obligations"; the prior "without exception" that neutralised 21.3 has been removed.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "breach of confidentiality... obligations", now carved out of the 21.1 cap.
21.3 Excluded Claims includes "gross negligence"; excepted from the cap by revised 21.1.
21.3 Excluded Claims includes "wilful misconduct"; excepted from the cap by revised 21.1.

reasons: Original 21.1 failed the fallback on two material terms: a one-month fee cap (below the 6-month walk-away floor) and "without exception", which overrode the 21.3 Excluded Claims and pulled indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct inside the cap. The "deviation" classification is correct.

The single replace to 21.1 achieves a complete fallback position: mutual cap, 12-month fee basis, and an "Except for Excluded Claims" hook onto the already-favourable 21.3 definition, which supplies the indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct carve-outs.

Preferred is not reached. Two defects remain in operative language: (i) 21.1 lacks the "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor and uses "actually paid" rather than "paid or payable", anchored to "the event" rather than the event giving rise to the claim; and (ii) 21.3's payment sentence covers only "undisputed Fees for conforming Services", a narrow subset of the s.1.5 Fees definition, so Customer's payment obligations generally are not excluded from capped damages.

Minimality holds: the edit changes only the cap basis and adds the Excluded Claims exception, deletes only the "without exception" language that defeats the carve-out elements, and adds no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category. Favourable retained text in 21.2 (mutual indirect-damages exclusion; restoration/replacement/notification/incident-response costs as direct damages) and 21.3 is untouched.

Intent is preserved: "Excluded Claims" was already defined in 21.3 and already referenced in 21.2, so the new cross-reference creates no undefined term or dangling reference, and no retained sentence contradicts the revised cap.

Optional preferred-level upgrade if negotiable: amend 21.1 to "the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000", and broaden the 21.3 payment sentence to all amounts due under the Agreement.
